name: Easy Yogurt Muffins
author: Clare de Boer
description: These muffins remove the pesky aspects of baking with kids without losing any of the joy. The batter is made entirely in a food processor, so you don’t have to worry about the delayed gratification of tempering butter or the potential burns that come with using the melted kind. There are plenty of opportunities to press buttons! The food processor also lets you skip processed sugar. This recipe uses dates instead, creaming them into the butter in the first step. You can let your kids go nuts decorating the tops with whatever they like (our favorite is blueberries) before sliding them into the oven. The resulting muffins are just sweet enough to qualify as a treat, and they're lovely enough for grown-ups, too. If you don’t have a food processor, finely chop the dates and have your kid smush them with a pestle and mortar before beating them into the butter by hand.

ingredients.raw: 8 tablespoons/113 grams unsalted butter, plus more for greasing the tin
ingredients.preparation: plus more for greasing the tin

ingredients.raw: ¾ cup whole-milk yogurt (preferably European style)
2 to 4 tablespoons maple syrup (depending on desired sweetness)
½ teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
1¾ cups/225 grams all-purpose flour, or another flour such as spelt or einkorn
ingredients.preparation: or another flour such as spelt or einkorn

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375 degrees. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin or line it with paper liners.

Place the butter, dates and eggs in the bowl of a food processor. Process until light and fluffy and the dates have nearly disappeared, 3 to 5 minutes. The mixture may look a little split but it will come back together.
Add the yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla, salt and cinnamon; process until smooth.
Add the flour, almond meal, flaxseed (if using), baking powder and baking soda. Pulse briefly, just until no dry flour remains. Do not overmix.
Divide the batter evenly among the prepared muffin cups (about ⅓ cup per muffin).
Decorate the muffin tops as you like, pressing the toppings lightly into the batter. Scatter some with berries, others with chopped nuts or rolled oats. Every muffin can be different.

Bake until the muffins are puffed, golden and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean, 22 to 25 minutes. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack. Muffins are best eaten the day they are baked, or can be frozen for a month or two.
